text:
sam: Hey @people-ops — quick scenario: my partner and I are traveling to Spain for 8 weeks after the baby is born (dates tentative: Dec 11 to Jan 25). I want to take company parental leave broken into: 4 weeks paid (US policy) then 4 weeks unpaid while in Spain. Questions: 1) Will my US paid leave still process if I'm physically in Spain? 2) Any payroll/tax withholding issues or paperwork for the unpaid Spain segment? 3) Does this affect my upcoming performance review (mid-Dec) or equity vesting schedule? 4) Can I keep my laptop and hotspot there?

michelle (People Ops): Congrats Sam! Short answers: 1) Paid leave should process as long as you're an active employee and manager approves the leave dates. 2) For cross-border stints, we need to evaluate payroll nexus; sometimes we require a short-term international payroll setup or a contractor invoice if employment abroad triggers local obligations. We'll route to Payroll for specifics. 3) Reviews still proceed on schedule; managers submit reviews regardless of leave. Equity vesting is governed by plan docs  typically vesting continues unless you terminate. We'll confirm. 4) IT travel ok with an equipment ticket and export clearance if required.

jules (Payroll): Hi Sam  two things: a) If you remain on US payroll while temporarily abroad (<=6 months typically), we usually continue US withholding but you must provide evidence of temporary travel and right-to-reside paperwork for Spain. b) If the stay is >90 days or you perform work (even occasional), local payroll registration might be required. Please complete the International Payroll Intake form and indicate remote-work days during the Spain segment.

an a (Manager): Sam  I'll approve the leave pending Sam's upload of docs. For the review: let's schedule a 30-min calibration in early Dec, but if you're on leave we'll still finalize goals and feedback. We can shift the calibration earlier if that helps.

sam: Thanks all. Are there specific docs Payroll needs for the "temporary abroad" case? Passport stamp? Flight itinerary? Lease?

jules (Payroll): Prefer passport copy, travel itinerary showing return date, and confirmation you're not entering local employment. If Spain needs it, we may also ask for a signed declaration of temporary assignment. I'll DM a checklist and the intake link.

michelle (People Ops): Policy snippet for reference:
```
Parental Leave (US employees): Eligible employees may take up to 12 weeks parental leave. Paid leave portion: up to 6 weeks at full pay depending on tenure. International travel while on leave: allowed but must be disclosed; cross-border work may trigger local payroll requirements.
```
Also: Benefits continuity (health insurance) continues for approved leave; please confirm payment arrangements if any premiums are due while abroad.

sam: Not planning to work while on the unpaid Spain weeks, but might check email occasionally. Does that count as working?

jules (Payroll): Casual email checks are usually fine, but active work (paid tasks, coding, supporting prod incidents) can create a local employment presence. If you expect to take any paid shifts, tell us so we can model tax impact.

it-bot: IT note: Equipment travel request required. Start an Equipment Travel ticket at https://redwood.internal/it/equipment-travel. Allow 10+ business days for export paperwork.

sam: Filed the parental leave form and attached passport + draft itinerary (ticket ref: 7Y2X). Opened Equipment Travel ticket IT-5621.

jules (Payroll): Got the intake. We'll run an initial risk check by Dec 1 and confirm whether we can keep US payroll unchanged. If a local registration is needed, Payroll will coordinate next steps and advise on gross-up or withholding differences.

michelle (People Ops): Action items: Sam  finalize leave dates and keep docs updated; Jules  run payroll nexus check and post back; Ana  schedule review calibration before Dec 10 if possible. We will not pause the review or equity vesting by default.

an a (Manager): I'll invite Sam to a 30-min review prep on Dec 6 at 10am. Sam if that conflicts because of travel, let me know and we'll move it earlier.

sam: Will do  really appreciate the clarity. I'll update dates by Nov 10. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

payroll-bot: Reminder: complete International Payroll Intake by Nov 12 to meet processing timelines for Dec payroll.
